title: Access modifiers
hook: Accessibility is metadata the CLR enforces. TypeScript private evaporates. C# private is a runtime no. Name every modifier, including file, in interviews.

sections.heading: The set you must recite
sections.prose: public: any assembly. private: containing type only (default for members). internal: same assembly (default for top-level types). protected: containing type and derived types. protected internal: same assembly or derived types in other assemblies (union). private protected: derived types that are also in the same assembly (intersection). file: the declaring source file only, for top-level types — source generators use it so HiddenWidget in two generated files do not collide.

sections.heading: What InternalsVisibleTo and file change
sections.prose: Test assemblies often use InternalsVisibleTo to reach internal types without making them public. That is still an assembly-level hole, not a language backdoor. file-local types cannot appear as public return types on non-file types. Nested types inherit a default of private, which surprises people coming from Java’s nested classes. Encapsulation of an auth parser’s signing key material is a private field, not a comment.

snippets.label: protected internal versus private protected versus file
snippets.explanation: TokenParser is internal to the assembly. Describe is visible to the assembly and to further derived types elsewhere. ParserHelpers is invisible outside this file.

sections.heading: Design rule
sections.prose: Public surface is a compatibility contract. Internal is for the application’s own composition. private is the default you should keep. protected is a promise to derived types — if you do not intend inheritance, sealed plus private is clearer (module 05).

interviewTakeaways: Members default private; types default internal.
protected internal is OR; private protected is AND.
file is file-local types, mainly for generators.
commonPitfalls: Confusing protected internal with private protected.
Shipping public DTOs that were meant to be internal implementation records.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS private is erased; ECMAScript #fields are a runtime hurdle but not CLR accessibility. C# modifiers survive in metadata and are checked by the runtime.
JS modules hide unbound names by not exporting them. That is file/module scope, closest to C# internal/file, not to CLR private on a member.
